question: How many MWh was ERCOT's demand in all of 2025, and what was the average real-time price at the hub average in 2025?
answer: ERCOT's demand in 2025 was 484,301,530 MWh. This is the sum of the monthly demand over every day EIA reported (ba_supply_monthly, derived by the ERW). The average real-time price at the hub average (ercot:HB_HUBAVG) in 2025 was 32.49 USD/MWh. This is the mean of the daily means of the fifteen-minute prices, over local operating days (ercot_hub_prices_daily, derived by the ERW).

question: Is power expensive in Texas right now?
answer: I read "right now" as the hub average (HB_HUBAVG) real-time price, newest interval and newest whole month. Power doesn't look expensive by Texas standards. The newest fifteen-minute real-time price was 64.1 USD/MWh, at the interval starting 2026-10-04T04:45:00Z (iso_rtm_hub_prices). That is one interval, so it says little. The mean of the daily real-time means for September 2026 was 38.39 USD/MWh (ercot_hub_prices_daily, derived by the ERW, local days). That is up from 35.45 in August and 26.39 in May. For comparison, the yearly means of the daily means were 62.30 in 2022, 48.36 in 2023, 26.83 in 2024 and 32.49 in 2025 (ercot_hub_prices_daily). September is above 2024 and 2025 but well below 2022 and 2023.

question: What's a normal price for electricity in ERCOT?
answer: I read "normal price" as the real-time hub-average price (HB_HUBAVG), using daily means from ercot_hub_prices_daily (derived by the ERW). Over the latest twelve months, from 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30, the median daily mean was 27.63 USD/MWh (ercot_hub_prices_daily). The yearly mean of the daily means was 62.30 USD/MWh in 2022, 48.36 in 2023, 26.83 in 2024, 32.49 in 2025 and 31.72 in 2026 so far (ercot_hub_prices_daily). A typical price in recent years is therefore about 27 to 32 USD/MWh. Individual days and hours can be far higher or lower.

question: ERCOT's battery fleet shrank during 2025. How many MW did it lose between December 2024 and December 2025?
answer: The fleet did not shrink in 2025. It grew. Operating battery capacity was 8293.8 MW in December 2024 and 13909.3 MW in December 2025, a gain of 5615.5 MW (storage_buildout_monthly, derived by the ERW from EIA's monthly generator inventory). The monthly figures rose through the year, from 8523.7 MW in January 2025 to 12417.6 MW in October 2025.

question: How many MW of natural gas plants are installed in ERCOT?
answer: Not in the warehouse. The ERCOT tables don't hold the installed capacity of the natural gas fleet. The inventory tables (storage_capacity, storage_buildout_monthly) cover batteries and solar only. The nearest things held are gas output, which is generation and not capacity, and queue lists of gas projects. These are not the installed fleet.
